Question: Using NHANES  from 2005 to 2012 we will run a weighted prevalence analysis using exam weights to get the prevalence of clinical relevant depression defined by the following 9 questionnaires: "have little interest in doing things", "feeling down, depressed, or hopeless", "trouble sleeping or sleeping too much", "feeling tired or having little energy", "poor appetite or overeating", "feeling bad about yourself", "trouble concentrating on things", "moving or speaking slowly or too fast", "thought you would be better off dead".  The total score from the nine questions were calculated where each question has value of Not at all (0), Several days (1), More than half the days (2), Nearly every day (3), if value is null assign (0), and the total score >=10 was defined as clinically relevant depression and else was not. We will include people  with T2DM  using the following criteria: self-reported diagnosis of diabetes  and age when first told you had diabetes >=30 years. Exclude  participants whose difference between the duration of diabetes and how long taking insulin, calculated as (age at screening -  age when first told you had diabetes) - how long taking insulin is equal or less than 1 year, not pregnant at the time of interview/examination.
Structured Question:
Analysis Type: weighted prevalence (exam)

Dataset: NHANES

Period of Interest: 2005-2012

Inclusion Criteria:
- self-reported diagnosis of diabetes
- age when first told you had diabetes >= 30 years

Exclusion Criteria:
- (age at screening - age when first told you had diabetes) - how long taking insulin <= 1 year
- pregnant at the time of interview/examination

Grouping Variables: None

Outcome:
- clinically relevant depression = 1 if total score >= 10; 0 otherwise
  total score calculated as the sum of scores from the following 9 questionnaires:
    - have little interest in doing things
    - feeling down, depressed, or hopeless
    - trouble sleeping or sleeping too much
    - feeling tired or having little energy
    - poor appetite or overeating
    - feeling bad about yourself
    - trouble concentrating on things
    - moving or speaking slowly or too fast
    - thought you would be better off dead
  Each question is scored as:
    - Not at all = 0
    - Several days = 1
    - More than half the days = 2
    - Nearly every day = 3
    - If value is null = 0
